title: observability: token+kv logging, metrics & dashboards + alert tuning
author: Rina Gupta
description: Adds token-level and KV-cache level logging hooks, new aggregated Prometheus metrics, Grafana dashboards, and alert tuning to better surface serving cost and latency regressions. Motivation: recent incidents and internal evaluations showed regressions that only appeared at token and KV-cache granularity (prefix-cache misses and expanded KV sizes). This PR introduces (1) structured token-level log entries emitted for sampled requests, (2) new Prometheus counters and histograms that expose per-route token-cost, per-token latency buckets, KV cache hit/miss ratios and KV size distribution, (3) Grafana dashboards for cost/latency breakdown and KV cache diagnostics, and (4) tuned alert rules targeting the new metrics with staged severities and playbook links. Implementation notes: added a lightweight sampling layer to avoid full trace volume increase, implemented label cardinality limits and tag normalization, instrumented runtime cache + scheduler code paths, and added migration notes for existing dashboards. Testing: unit tests for metric label behavior, integration run in perf-canary showing no >0.5% p99 latency regression at 95th percentile traffic, staged rollout to dedicated clusters with feature flags. Rollout plan: enable metrics under feature flag for 48h in canary, then enable read-only dashboards for internal SRE, then enable alerts in low-severity mode for one week before full severity. Related: ENG-1892 (kv-cache diagnostics) and SUP-4128 (support case tracing).

review_conversation: Lena Park requested changes: limit label cardinality on route_name and model_id, and add explicit example in docs for tag normalization.
Rina Gupta (author) reply: added label sanitization util and updated docs with examples; reduced route_name to route_hash when cardinality > 1000.
Mateo Ruiz comment: alert thresholds look aggressive for tail-heavy workloads; suggested staged severity and a cooldown window.
Rina Gupta reply: implemented staged severity (info->warning->critical) with 15m cooldown and added playbook links for escalation.
Ava Thompson approval: Verified dashboards in our canary org and smoke-tested alerts in low-severity mode.
testing_summary: Unit tests added for label sanitization and sampling; integration against perf-canary executed with no measurable p99 regression (>0.5%) and KV cache metrics validated; dashboards previewed with internal data; alerts validated in low-sev mode during canary window.
release_notes: Instrument token-level cost and latency metrics, KV-cache diagnostics, Grafana dashboards, and tuned alerts. Feature gated rollout; enable via canary flag before full rollout.
rollout_plan: 1) Enable feature flag in perf-canary for 48h. 2) Expose dashboards to SRE/observability team. 3) Enable alerts in low-severity mode for 7 days. 4) Promote to dedicated and hosted tiers with monitoring of false positives for 2 weeks.
notes: Cardinality limits required manual review; Ops to monitor storage impact during first 2 weeks.
